name: Flamingo Gardens
title: Ancient Trees in Flamingo Gardens: 12 to Find
meta_description: Florida's champion cluster fig, strangler fig, earpod and bodhi tree share one garden in Davie, west of Fort Lauderdale. Where to find each record tree.
intro: Flamingo Gardens says its cluster fig is the largest tree in Florida's whole champion register, and the state's tape and the garden's own disagree only on whether the trunk is 14 or 16 metres round. The garden began as the Wray family's homestead in 1927 and grew into a botanical garden and wildlife sanctuary in Davie, west of Fort Lauderdale, with 23 Florida champion trees by Wikipedia's count. Most of the record holders came from elsewhere in the tropics. An earpod tree from Central America is over six metres round, a sandbox tree throws its seed up to thirty metres when the pods burst, and a bodhi tree, the species Buddhist tradition honours at Bodh Gaya, stands by the parrot enclosure. The two strangler figs are natives, 110 metres apart, and the one that lost the state title is the taller. The gumbo limbo is the other local, short and unusually thick. Nobody recorded when any of them went in, so this is a garden of girths rather than ages. Entry is paid, and the narrated tram passes the rainforest stretch.
